entries.title: Setup builds a shared zoo system and a personal action row
entries.summary: Prepare the shared board, Break track, display, Association board, project and final-scoring supplies, then give each player a zoo map, five action cards, counters, workers, money, and the specified starting cards and pieces. Player count changes some starting placements, so use the selected edition’s setup diagram for exact quantities.

entries.title: Rounds alternate individual turns with administrative breaks
entries.summary: Players take turns by choosing one action card, resolving that action, and rotating the chosen card to the weakest slot. The Break track determines when administration interrupts play; breaks refresh selected supplies and workers, advance upkeep, and set up the next cycle. Continue until the end condition is reached, then resolve final scoring.

source_locator.document_section: Gameplay; The Break Track; A Turn / The 5 Action Cards
source_locator.locator: Gameplay; The Break Track; A Turn / The 5 Action Cards; pp. 6–9, 18

entries.title: Action-card position is the strength and timing control
entries.summary: The selected action’s slot supplies its current strength. Resolve the action using that strength, including any required minimums and any effects that trigger during or after the action; then shift the row and return the used card to the first slot. Do not treat the five action types as a fixed round order—the player chooses the card each turn.

source_locator.locator: A Turn / The 5 Action Cards; pp. 8–9

entries.title: Association workers occupy contested tasks; no generic exploration action is assumed
entries.summary: Association workers are committed to tasks on the Association board, where task availability and the action strength determine whether the placement can resolve. A break recalls and refreshes the player’s workers. The base-game sections identify association work rather than a general exploration track or exploration action, so questions using exploration terminology—especially from an expansion or another game—must be checked against the intended edition.

source_locator.locator: Association; The Association Board; Break; pp. 14–16, 18

entries.title: Money, tokens, cards, and zoo components are separate resource classes
entries.summary: Ark Nova’s economy combines money with appeal, conservation, reputation, Break, and X-token tracking, while cards and physical zoo components provide actions, animals, sponsors, projects, buildings, partner zoos, and universities. Treat a named item or “artifact” as a component-specific question rather than inventing a universal artifact resource: its cost, icon, timing, and effect require the exact current component reference.

entries.title: Guardian terminology is outside the verified base procedure set
entries.summary: The uploaded base-game rulebook’s core procedure is organized around zoo actions, association workers, animals, sponsors, projects, and administration breaks; it does not establish a generic guardian subsystem in the covered sections. If a card, scenario, expansion, or translation names a guardian, do not infer its effect from this corpus—use an authorized current reference or return not_yet_covered.

entries.title: Universities provide research-style infrastructure through association work
entries.summary: Association work can add universities to the zoo. These tiles provide the icons, reputation, and other benefits they show, and their placement changes which future association and card requirements can be met. The strategic interpretation is to treat university acquisition as an infrastructure investment; exact university icons and bonuses remain component-specific.

entries.title: The game ends when the appeal and conservation races intersect
entries.summary: Track appeal and conservation separately during play. When a player’s two counters meet, the end sequence is triggered after the remaining turns are handled as specified; then resolve the displayed final-scoring objectives and compare final values. Exact objective conditions, card points, ties, and edition-specific adjustments belong to the current scoring reference rather than this paraphrase.
